transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is... I've been having this issue with how much I'm eating. Especially on late work nights. I’ll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner, but it usually turns into a whole entrée, sides, dessert... and then I'll even grab extra snacks from my kitchen on top of that. It's just way, way more food than I’d ever eat if someone were sitting across from me.
During these episodes when you're eating all that food late at night, do you feel like you can't stop or control how much you're eating, even if you want to?

Yeah, that's exactly it. Once I start, there's this point where I'm almost just... watching myself keep going. I'll be opening another package or going back for more, and in my head I'm thinking that I really should stop. But it just feels like the decision has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't seem to stop myself.
After these episodes where you eat a lot, do you do anything to try to compensate or make up for it—like making yourself vomit, using laxatives, exercising excessively, or fasting the next day?

No, I don't do any of that. I just... I usually just feel really awful about myself afterwards. But I don't throw up or take anything, and I definitely don't exercise a lot. I might skip breakfast the next day because I'm still so full, but I don't try to fast on purpose to make up for it.
How often would you say these episodes of eating a lot happen? Is it something that occurs multiple times a week, once a week, a few times a month, or less frequently?

Well, um, I actually looked back at my delivery receipts and my calendar recently to kind of track it. There’s usually at least one night every week where this happens... sometimes more, depending on work. But definitely at least once a week. And that pattern has been going on for several months now.

When you think about these eating episodes and how they've been affecting your life, how much distress or upset do they cause you? And has this pattern impacted things like your work, relationships, or how you feel about yourself?

It definitely causes a lot of distress. I feel really upset and... just ashamed of myself after it happens. It really drags down my self-esteem. As for work or relationships, um... I haven't really noticed a huge impact on my work, other than maybe being a bit sluggish the next morning. And with relationships, I mostly just keep it to myself and hide it. So it's more that it just makes me feel really awful about myself on the inside.

When you think about the amount of food you eat during these episodes—compared to what most people would eat in a similar situation—would you say you're eating an unusually large amount of food, or does it just feel out of control even though the quantity might be more normal?

It's definitely an unusually large amount. When I have these late work nights, I'll order what I tell myself is just going to be dinner. But then it turns into a whole entrée, a bunch of sides, dessert, and then I'll even grab extra snacks from my kitchen on top of that. 

It's way more food than I would ever eat if someone were sitting across the table from me. So, yeah, it's not just the feeling of being out of control—the actual quantity is a lot more than what would be normal for one meal.

You mentioned you might skip breakfast the next day because you're still full—but I want to clarify: have you ever intentionally restricted your eating or exercised heavily on purpose specifically to try to undo or compensate for one of these eating episodes, or is that something you've never done?

No, I don't really do anything like that to make up for it. I mean, I might skip breakfast like I said, but that's just because my stomach hurts or I'm genuinely not hungry yet. I don't force myself to fast, and I definitely don't go to the gym and exercise for hours to burn it off or anything. I just kind of wake up feeling terrible and try to move on with the day.

During these eating episodes, when you're eating all that food, would you describe it more as: you're making a conscious choice to keep eating even though you know you should stop, or is it more like you genuinely feel like you've lost control and can't stop yourself even if you really wanted to in that moment?

It's definitely a loss of control. I'm not... I'm not just deciding to keep eating. Once I start, there's this point where I'm almost just watching myself do it. Like, I'll be clicking to order more food, or opening another package, and in my head I'm thinking, "I really need to stop this," but it feels like the actual ability to stop has already slipped out of my hands. I just can't make myself stop, even though I want to.

I want to make sure I have this right—when you say you don't do anything to compensate, I'm asking about all the ways someone might try to counteract a binge. Beyond vomiting, laxatives, and exercise, have you ever used diet pills, diuretics, or any other methods to try to prevent weight gain after these episodes?

No, I've never used any of those either. No diet pills, no diuretics, nothing like that. Like I said, I just kind of deal with feeling awful the next day, but I don't try to use anything to fix it or stop the weight gain.
